rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant outside the process is asked to carry out a piece of work, and a later step is described as following the completion of that work, with no message, signal, timer or condition named as the thing the process waits for: Model the requested work as a task (a manual task when it is done without a system) placed in the sequence where the description places it, after the step that requests it. Model the request itself as a send step, and use an intermediate catch event only for an explicitly described message, signal, timer or condition. Do not replace the performed work with a catch event that names its completion.
rules.situation: the description states that a participant outside the process is asked to carry out a piece of work, and a later step is described as following the completion of that work, with no message, signal, timer or condition named as the thing the process waits for

rules.instruction: When the description names a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would use a different verb, a synonym, a restated object, or extra words such as a recipient, a reaction, or a circumstance that the description does not attach to that activity's own action: Label the task with the verb and object words that the description uses for that activity, in the same order and without synonyms or added qualifiers. Model any circumstance, reaction, or recipient that the description states separately as an event, a gateway branch, or the sequence flow leading to the task.
rules.situation: the description states a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would append a recipient, a qualifying phrase, or a restated object that the description attaches to a different step or does not attach to the activity

rules.instruction: When the description says a participant sends a request or order to one or more outside participants that do not perform the rest of the process, and one or more of those outside participants later send an item back that the participant waits for before continuing: Model each outside participant as its own bpmn:participant pool in the collaboration. Place the sending task in the requesting participant's pool and draw a message flow from that task to the outside pool. Model each wait for a returned item as an intermediate catch event in the requesting participant's pool, and draw a message flow from the outside pool to that catch event, so that the direction of every message matches the description. When the description says the participant continues only after several such items have arrived, join the waiting branches with a parallel gateway before the next step.
rules.situation: the description says a participant sends a request or order to one or more outside participants that do not perform the rest of the process, and one or more of those outside participants later send an item back that the participant waits for before continuing

rules.instruction: When the description says that an actor, after deriving a list of items from a plan, places a manual purchase of those items with one or more external vendors, and then describes other actions as running while that purchase is pending: Model the manual purchase as a user task in the actor's lane. Place it directly after the task that creates the item list and before the parallel gateway that starts the concurrent actions. Connect the list task to the purchase task, and connect the purchase task to that parallel gateway. Do not model a manual purchase as a send task, and do not connect the list task directly to the parallel gateway.
rules.situation: the description says that an actor, after deriving a list of items from a plan, places a manual purchase of those items with one or more external vendors, and then describes other actions as running while that purchase is pending

rules.instruction: When the description says a person places orders with external suppliers through a software system or web-based shop for items the person needs, and the ordering is an action the person carries out before the process continues: Model the placing of such orders as a user task (userTask) in the lane of the person who performs them, placed in the sequence where the description places the ordering. Do not model that ordering action as a send task, because a send task is reserved for cases where sending a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
rules.situation: the description says a person places orders with external suppliers through a software system or web-based shop for items the person needs, and the ordering is an action the person carries out before the process continues
